records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
A J-1 master's student can do up to **18 months** of Academic Training (AT), or the length of their degree program, whichever is shorter. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension. ([ISSS Academic Training page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment))

Key conditions:
- AT done while you're studying and AT done after your program ends are added together toward the limit.
- Full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- The total employment/training period can't exceed the length of your academic program.
- AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date, and it must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- To apply, submit the Academic Training form (on the ISSS Student Portal) to ISSS at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends submitting at least three weeks ahead to leave time for processing.

**Possible change to be aware of:** DHS published a final rule on July 17, 2026 eliminating "duration of status," which would affect people who need extra time for post-completion training. However, on September 14, 2026, a federal court postponed its effective date and barred DHS from implementing it, according to [the ISSS update](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status). ISSS is monitoring the situation.

For details on your own case, including the STEM extension, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.
